## Claude (Anthropic)
- **Company**: Anthropic
- **Claim**: State-of-the-art agentic coding assistant
- **Benchmark scores**: Claude Mythos Preview 93.9% SWE-bench Verified; Claude Opus 4.8 88.6% SWE-bench Verified; ~3.0% ProgramBench partial credit (Claude Opus 4.7, 95%+ pass rate on some tasks)
- **Approach**: Cloud-based, 1M token context, multi-file agentic reasoning
- **Compiler verification**: Not a core mechanism — relies on agentic reasoning and code execution
- **ProgramBench full resolution**: 0% (no model breaks the cleanroom metric)
- **Relevant to**: All Determinex pitches — Claude is both a tool Determinex uses AND a competitor at the benchmark level

## OpenAI (GPT-5.x series)
- **Company**: OpenAI / Microsoft
- **Claim**: Leading code generation with agent-driven fuzzing
- **Benchmark scores**: GPT-5.5 82.7% Terminal-Bench 2.0, 58.6% SWE-bench Pro; GPT-5.3-Codex 57% SWE-bench Pro
- **Approach**: Cloud-based agentic coding; uses fuzzing with 248,853+ hidden tests in ProgramBench
- **Compiler verification**: Agent-driven behavioral testing (not compiler-gated)
- **ProgramBench full resolution**: Sole model to partially crack a single task at full resolution
- **Determinex differentiation**: OpenAI fuzz-tests but doesn't gate on compiler pass; Determinex's compiler oracle is deterministic

## Devin (Cognition AI)
- **Company**: Cognition
- **Claim**: "First AI software engineer" — autonomous multi-step coding agent
- **Benchmark scores**: 13.86% SWE-bench (self-reported); 2/7 on internal real-world tasks (47 min avg vs 18 min human)
- **Approach**: Autonomous sandboxed agent with shell + browser + code editor; excels at legacy refactoring (COBOL→Rust)
- **Compiler verification**: Sandboxed validation only — no compiler oracle
- **Determinex differentiation**: Devin works well on bounded tasks with clear specs. Determinex trains on failures; Devin doesn't self-improve.

## ProgramBench Context (The Only Benchmark That Matters for Determinex)

ProgramBench requires **cleanroom reconstruction** of real software (FFmpeg, SQLite, PHP, tinycc)
from compiled executable + docs only, with zero internet access. The official metric:
`passed == total, not_run == 0, failed == 0`.

**Current public frontier scores: 0-0.5% fully resolved.**

Determinex's confirmed score (corrected 2026-06-30): **0/200** under the strict official
metric (passed==total, 0 not_run) — a full provenance audit found the prior "64/200 =
32.0%" claim counted upstream source builds, not native reimplementations. This matches
public leaderboard reality. The 62 archived builds are retained as reference corpus for
the Native Reimplementation Loop, the legitimate path to a real lock. See
`docs/papers/PROGRAMBENCH.md`'s correction banner for evidence.

---

## Determinex's Unique Position

Determinex is the only AI coding system that combines four properties simultaneously:
(1) **compiler-verified outputs** — every generated patch must pass `rustc`/`go`/`python`/`tsc`
before it enters the training corpus, making hallucination impossible to propagate;
(2) **self-improving closed loop** — every failure with its exact error + fix becomes labeled
training data, meaning the system gets measurably better from production use;
(3) **privacy-sovereign operation** — Project Cloak lets cloud AI assist on local code without
ever seeing real identifiers, enabling enterprise use without IP leakage;
(4) **ProgramBench leadership at 7.5% resolved** under the strict official metric, while all
public frontier models (Claude, GPT-5.5, Gemini) score 0-0.5% on the same standard.

No competitor addresses all four simultaneously. Most address zero.
